title: Termwise epicification by bounded flat contractible disks
statement: Let E,H be bounded-above cochain complexes of module sheaves on a small ringed site, E termwise flat, and f:E -> H any chain map. Suppose every module sheaf has an epimorphism from a flat module sheaf. There exist a bounded-above termwise flat complex F and maps s:E -> F and g:F -> H such that s is a quasi-isomorphism, g is termwise epic, and s followed by g equals f strictly. No quasi-isomorphism property of f or g is assumed or asserted. [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]

proof.text: Fix an upper bound N for H. For each i <= N choose, using the explicitly assumed cover property, a flat epimorphism p_i:P_i -> H^i. For i > N use P_i=0, which is flat by tensor closedness. Form the identity disk on P_i in degrees i and i+1. Their sum has degree j term P_j plus P_(j-1), differential sending the first summand identically to the second in degree j+1 and killing the second. A contracting homotopy sends the second summand to the first in degree j-1. These formulas directly verify differential squared zero and dh+hd=identity.

The disk augmentations have components p_i and p_i followed by d_H. Together they give a chain map a:D -> H, epic in every degree: its P_i restriction is p_i for i<=N, and H^i is zero otherwise. Set F=E plus D, take the inclusion s:E -> F, and g=[f,a]. Thus s followed by g equals f and g is termwise epic. Projection onto E and the contracting homotopy of D show that s is a homotopy equivalence, hence quasi-isomorphic. The terms of F are finite sums of flat terms; F is bounded by the maximum of a bound for E and N+1.

mathlib_searches.query: relative cone replacement; adding contractible flat disks for termwise epimorphic augmentation

mathlib_searches.results: mappingCone, fst, snd, inl, inr, descCochain, liftCochain and isZero_X_iff; tools for construction, no relative flat extension or flat disk augmentation theorem.

No matching flat relative extension or flat epicification theorem. Mathlib CM5a/CM5b use injectives and lower bounds; unsuitable. Project bounded flat replacements are the existing source of the cone replacement.
